name: Hiring
description: An applicant tracking system: requisitions with approvals and openings, an application portal at a direct link with pay ranges and privacy notices, an application-review queue, a pipeline by stage with bulk actions, per-job interview plans and kits, structured scorecards, self-scheduling links with calendar invites, offers with approvals and a candidate accept/decline link, referrals, prospect pools, email templates, reports with the industry's standard formulas, voluntary self-ID readable only by a compliance role, and retention rules that anonymize candidates automatically. Add your own questions, stages and reasons without losing updates.
changelog:
2.1.0 — per-job access: a job's applications, interviews, notes, scorecards and offers are seen by its hiring team (hiring manager, recruiter, coordinator, interviewers) and by anyone an interview or approval names, and a confidential job by its team alone; recruiters see everything. Recruiter is now a role for workspace admins and people given it by name, not every editor. The compliance role reads applications for self-ID totals. Rejection emails can wait a day or three, and are cancelled if the candidate is un-rejected first. Reject a candidate from all their applications at once; cancel interviews in bulk; a referral links to the application it became.

2.0.0 — a full applicant tracker, built from public ATS research: job approvals, openings and requisition IDs, pay ranges (required by Massachusetts law) and a JobPosting feed for Google and job boards, privacy notices, voluntary self-ID for a compliance role only, an application-review queue, bulk reject with per-candidate emails, stage history, notes, per-job interview plans and kits, structured scorecards, availability links candidates pick a time from, calendar invites, offers with approvals and an accept/decline link, mark hired closing the opening, referrals, prospect pools, email templates, reports, retention by region with legal hold. 1.0.0 — jobs, careers page, applications with résumé upload, pipeline, interviews, scorecards, reject with reason (and email), reports.

listing.tagline: An applicant tracker for the whole hiring loop: jobs, applications, interviews, offers and reports, in your workspace.
listing.overview:
Hiring runs recruiting end to end inside canopy. Recruiters open jobs from templates, get them approved, and post them to an application portal at a direct link. Applications land in a review queue; the pipeline shows every candidate by stage, with bulk moves and rejections. Interviewers get a kit and a scorecard for each interview; candidates pick an interview time and accept their offer through private links, with no account.

It keeps candidates' data the way the law asks: pay ranges on every posting, privacy notices whose version is recorded, voluntary self-ID questions only one role can read, and candidates anonymized automatically after a period you set by region. A job's candidates are seen by its hiring team, and a confidential search by its team alone.

Like every canopy app, it is yours once installed: add fields, stages, wording or whole pages, test the change on a copy, and keep receiving the template's updates.
listing.audience: People Ops and recruiters run it; hiring managers and interviewers see the jobs they work on; every employee can refer someone. Candidates never need a canopy account.
listing.data: Jobs, openings and approvals; candidates (name, contact details, résumé, answers, stage history, notes, scorecards, offers); referrals and talent pools. Self-ID answers are readable only by the compliance role and are reported as totals. Rejected candidates are anonymized after 180 days (EU/UK) or 365 days (US) unless on legal hold — both are settings. Nothing is emailed until the server's app email is switched on.

highlights.title: Jobs with approvals
highlights.body: Start from a template, add openings with IDs, and route the job to approvers. It stays a draft until the last one approves. A pay range is required before it opens.

highlights.title: An application portal at a link
highlights.body: Open, live, non-confidential jobs appear at your workspace's careers link, with pay ranges, a privacy notice and an accommodation contact. Google for Jobs data and an XML feed for job boards come with it.

highlights.title: Review queue and pipeline
highlights.body: Work through new applications one at a time with keyboard shortcuts and duplicate warnings, then move or reject candidates in bulk. Each rejection email is filled in for its own candidate, and can wait a day.

highlights.title: Interviews, kits and scorecards
highlights.body: Per-job interview plans give each interviewer the questions and the attributes to rate. Candidates choose from times you offer through a private link; everyone gets a calendar invite.

highlights.title: Offers
highlights.body: Draft an offer, get it approved, send it; the candidate accepts or declines through a private link. Marking them hired closes the opening.

highlights.title: Per-job access
highlights.body: A job's candidates are seen by its hiring team and by whoever interviews them; a confidential job is hidden from everyone else. Recruiters see everything.

highlights.title: Reports
highlights.body: Pipeline now and ever, pass-through rates, days in stage, time to hire and to fill, source of hire and offer acceptance, using the standard ATS definitions.

highlights.title: Privacy built in
highlights.body: Retention rules anonymize candidates on a schedule by region, respect a legal hold, and an admin can export everything held about one person.

recruiter.description: Opens jobs, moves and rejects candidates, schedules interviews, makes offers, and sees every job. Workspace admins hold it; give it to others by name.

interviewer.description: Sees the candidates of the jobs they are on the hiring team of (or interview for), their interview kits, and writes scorecards. Grant it to a viewer who interviews.

compliance.description: Reads voluntary self-identification answers, as totals only. Grant it to People Ops or legal — never to a hiring team.

careers_intro.label: Application portal introduction
careers_intro.default: We build open-source technology that helps frontline workers deliver better services in over 80 countries. Come help.

accommodation_contact.label: Who applicants ask for an accommodation
accommodation_contact.help: Shown on every job: 'Need an accommodation to apply? Email …'

privacy_notice.label: Applicant privacy notice
privacy_notice.help: Shown before an applicant submits. Say what you collect, why, who sees it, how long you keep it and how to ask for it to be deleted.
privacy_notice.default: We use the information you give us only to consider you for this and similar roles. Our hiring team and the people who interview you can see it. We keep applications for up to 12 months (6 months in the EU and UK) unless you agree to stay in our talent pool, then remove them. To see, correct or delete your data, email people@dimagi.com.

privacy_notice_version.label: Privacy notice version
privacy_notice_version.help: Change it whenever you change the notice; each application records the version its applicant saw.

ask_self_id.label: Ask US applicants the voluntary self-identification questions

require_pay_range.label: A job cannot open without a pay range
require_pay_range.help: Massachusetts (and several other states) require a good-faith pay range on every posting.

team_only_access.label: Only a job's hiring team sees its candidates
team_only_access.help: Off: every interviewer sees the candidates of every non-confidential job. Confidential jobs are always team-only.

Hi {{name}},

Thank you for applying for {{job.title}} at {{settings.company_name}}. We read every application and will be in touch.

The {{settings.company_name}} hiring team

rejection_body.label: Rejection email
rejection_body.default:

Thank you for your interest in {{job.title}} at {{settings.company_name}}. After careful consideration we have decided not to move forward with your application.

We wish you the best,
The {{settings.company_name}} hiring team

{{link}}

The {{settings.company_name}} hiring team

The {{settings.company_name}} hiring team
